failures.message: ran and passed with its mutant applied to saffron/end_review.py — A layer the resolver cannot place gets `error` on both its lenses at cost 0, and the walk goes on to the layer below. There are two outcomes. Its own branch is gone at origin, driven on a bottom layer and on one with a predecessor. Its current head contains none of its candidate bases, driven on a layer with a predecessor and on two bottom layers. One bottom layer was force-pushed onto unrelated history. The other was rebased below the commit PACKAGE built it on, so its merge base with the default branch does not descend from that commit. A layer whose predecessor is a stack base with a gone branch, and whose head does not contain that recorded head, is driven too. Each error names the layer's branch. The second outcome also names the current head and every candidate, and any predecessor branch found gone. The join is filed `error` at cost 0 when any layer fails, at the bottom, the top or the middle of a stack. A failed fetch is not cached. Each resolution that needs that branch fetches it again and raises again, which the witness counts for a gone bottom branch.

payload.summary: 1 of 2 witness(es) survived their own mutant
